questions.question: An IPv6-only client receives a synthetic AAAA but never reaches WAN. What should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: The DHCPv6 lease timer on the client-facing interface
options.feedback: Lease duration affects renewal, not the synthetic destination match.

options.label: B
options.text: The IPv4 static route to the ISP next hop
options.feedback: Routing matters later; first confirm the synthetic address matches VIP6.

options.label: C
options.text: The VIP6 range and embedded-IPv4 setting
options.feedback: VIP6 must cover the DNS64 prefix and decode its embedded IPv4 address.

options.label: D
options.text: The FortiGate system time and NTP status
options.feedback: Clock skew may affect logs, not this address match.

questions.question: A service has native AAAA and A records, but DNS64 keeps synthesizing. Which setting changes selection?

options.label: A
options.text: Disable always-synthesize-aaaa-record in system dns64
options.feedback: DNS64 then checks native AAAA and synthesizes only when absent.

options.label: B
options.text: Disable the IPv6 DHCP server on the client interface
options.feedback: DHCPv6 controls addressing, not DNS64 native-record preference.

options.label: C
options.text: Remove the IPv4 pool from the NAT64 policy
options.feedback: That breaks translation but does not change DNS answers.

options.label: D
options.text: Narrow the VIP6 extip range to one address
options.feedback: VIP6 affects packet matching after DNS resolution.

questions.question: The policy counter increments, but WAN capture lacks the intended translated source. What should be verified?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the client requested an A record instead
options.feedback: The client can use AAAA; the missing source points to pool selection.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether policy logging is enabled
options.feedback: Logging improves visibility but does not enable translation.

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the VIP6 object has a comment
options.feedback: Comments do not alter packet translation.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the IP pool has nat64 enabled and is selected
options.feedback: The pool must be NAT64-enabled and referenced by the matching policy.

questions.question: Which evidence best proves a NAT64 packet left WAN after translation?

options.label: A
options.text: The client resolver cache contains the synthetic AAAA
options.feedback: That proves synthesis, not forwarding.

options.label: B
options.text: A WAN capture shows IPv4 destination and pool source
options.feedback: The egress packet proves destination and source translation.

options.label: C
options.text: The IPv6 address object displays the correct prefix
options.feedback: That proves configuration, not packet forwarding.

options.label: D
options.text: The DNS proxy reports an upstream A response
options.feedback: That proves upstream resolution, not NAT64 egress.

questions.question: A firmware template includes FortiGate, switches, APs and Extenders. One managed switch is offline. What should happen?

options.label: A
options.text: All FortiGate upgrades stop before starting
options.feedback: The stop applies to later tasks in that device's fabric sequence.

options.label: B
options.text: FortiAP upgrades first, then waits for the switch
options.feedback: The documented order upgrades switches before APs.

options.label: C
options.text: That sequence stops at the offline switch
options.feedback: An offline child stops its remaining downstream sequence.

options.label: D
options.text: Every assigned FortiGate device is cancelled
options.feedback: Other assigned FortiGate devices can continue concurrently.

questions.question: No FortiExtender image appears in FortiGuard. What is the documented preparation?

options.label: A
options.text: Download from Support and import through FortiGuard module
options.feedback: FortiExtender images are manually imported into FortiManager.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable FortiGate alternate-partition boot for Extender
options.feedback: Alternate partition is a FortiGate option.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the template schedule to on-board
options.feedback: Scheduling does not supply a missing image.

options.label: D
options.text: Upgrade the FortiSwitch first to unlock the image
options.feedback: Switch order does not affect Extender image availability.

questions.question: A closed-network FortiManager cannot retrieve the recommended upgrade path. Which plan is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Select skip-intermediate and assume the path is cached
options.feedback: The path tool cannot supply missing images.

options.label: B
options.text: Reboot devices and retry the same template
options.feedback: A reboot does not import intermediate images.

options.label: C
options.text: Use any local image without platform validation
options.feedback: Images must match platform and upgrade path.

options.label: D
options.text: Import each required intermediate image and push in order
options.feedback: A closed network must stage the recommended images locally.

questions.question: An HA cluster has a down secondary while the all-members-up gate is enabled. What happens?

options.label: A
options.text: The primary upgrades and synchronizes the secondary later
options.feedback: The gate is designed to skip a cluster with a down member.

options.label: B
options.text: The cluster upgrade is skipped until all members are up
options.feedback: The HA gate prevents upgrade with an unavailable member.

options.label: C
options.text: The template changes to alternate-partition boot
options.feedback: Boot behavior is independent of HA eligibility.

options.label: D
options.text: The firmware image is deleted from the repository
options.feedback: A down member does not invalidate the image.

questions.question: Archive logs exist, but Log View has no results for that date range. What is the key distinction?

options.label: A
options.text: Archive and Analytics are separate; the logs may not be indexed
options.feedback: Log View uses Analytics; Archive stores raw files.

options.label: B
options.text: Archive files become searchable after changing the GUI filter
options.feedback: Archive browsing is not equivalent to Analytics queries.

options.label: C
options.text: The FortiGate must resend every historical log
options.feedback: A rebuild can index available archives without retransmission.

options.label: D
options.text: HA synchronization must be disabled before queries work
options.feedback: Archive synchronization and local indexing are separate.

questions.question: Two FortiAnalyzer HA nodes have different Analytics sizes but matching raw archives. What likely explains it?

options.label: A
options.text: They rebuilt Analytics from different start dates
options.feedback: Local rebuild windows can create different indexed ranges despite archive sync.

options.label: B
options.text: The heartbeat uses a different UDP port
options.feedback: Heartbeat transport does not explain local index range differences.

options.label: C
options.text: One member lost the FortiGate serial number
options.feedback: Matching raw archives show source data exists on both.

options.label: D
options.text: The larger database is automatically the active member
options.feedback: Database size is not an HA role-election criterion.

questions.question: An analyst needs reports for dates older than Analytics retention. What action is required?

options.label: A
options.text: Use Archive directly as the Reports data source
options.feedback: Archive is not the query-ready source for standard reports.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase the dashboard refresh interval
options.feedback: Refresh timing cannot create missing indexed rows.

options.label: C
options.text: Disable archive rolling and rerun the report
options.feedback: That changes future retention, not historical indexing.

options.label: D
options.text: Rebuild Analytics from the required archived date range
options.feedback: The requested archive range must be loaded into Analytics.

questions.question: Before rebuilding Analytics on both members, what should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: The dashboard theme and HA badge color
options.feedback: Presentation does not prove source-log availability.

options.label: B
options.text: Archive availability, ADOM quota and the same start date
options.feedback: A rebuild cannot restore files already trimmed from Archive.

options.label: C
options.text: FortiGate policy order for current log traffic
options.feedback: Policy order does not determine historical archive availability.

options.label: D
options.text: The administrator session label on each node
options.feedback: Session labels do not control retention or rebuild range.

questions.question: A FortiSwitch port receives superior BPDUs and must never become a path to root. Which guard fits?

options.label: A
options.text: BPDU guard on the edge port
options.feedback: BPDU guard protects an edge port from any BPDU.

options.label: B
options.text: Root guard on the protected non-root-facing port
options.feedback: Root guard blocks superior BPDUs and enters Root-Inconsistent.

options.label: C
options.text: Loop protection on the current root port
options.feedback: Loop protection is intended for nondesignated paths.

options.label: D
options.text: Disable STP on the protected uplink
options.feedback: Disabling STP removes loop prevention.

questions.question: An access port should connect only to an endpoint. What prerequisites apply before BPDU guard?

options.label: A
options.text: MST region changed and port set to trunk mode
options.feedback: Region identity does not replace edge-port prerequisites.

options.label: B
options.text: Root guard enabled globally and port made nondesignated
options.feedback: Root guard is a different protection mechanism.

options.label: C
options.text: Loop protection disabled and BPDU forwarding enabled
options.feedback: Those settings do not establish BPDU guard.

options.label: D
options.text: Global STP, interface STP and edge-port enabled
options.feedback: The guide requires all three settings.

questions.question: A nondesignated alternate port stops receiving expected BPDUs. Which protection should be examined?

options.label: A
options.text: Loop protection on the nondesignated port
options.feedback: It monitors expected BPDU loss on alternate/backup paths.

options.label: B
options.text: Root guard because a superior BPDU arrived
options.feedback: The scenario is missing expected BPDUs, not receiving superior ones.

options.label: C
options.text: BPDU guard because every missing BPDU shuts edge ports
options.feedback: BPDU guard reacts to received BPDUs on edge ports.

options.label: D
options.text: Edge-port fast forwarding on the distribution uplink
options.feedback: Edge-port behavior is not the nondesignated-path guard.

questions.question: Two switches expected in one MST region calculate different boundaries. Which consistency check matters first?

options.label: A
options.text: Local switch hostname and administrator profile
options.feedback: Those do not define MST region identity.

options.label: B
options.text: DHCP lease duration for each VLAN
options.feedback: DHCP timers do not define MSTP region membership.

options.label: C
options.text: Region name, revision and VLAN-to-instance mapping
options.feedback: All three must align for the same MST region.

options.label: D
options.text: Physical port description and LLDP system name
options.feedback: Those are inventory details, not region parameters.

questions.question: An AP is configured for Zero-Wait DFS, but the feature is unavailable. What should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the SSID uses WPA3 Enterprise
options.feedback: Client authentication does not establish radio capability.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether FortiAnalyzer has an Analytics ADOM
options.feedback: Analytics storage does not affect DFS support.

options.label: C
options.text: Supported model/radio combination and FortiAP release
options.feedback: Support is limited to specified hardware and FortiAP 7.6.3+.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the AP is connected to a 2.4-GHz-only profile
options.feedback: Zero-Wait DFS is a 5-GHz radio feature.

questions.question: In FCC/MKK, how does rCAC reduce the radar interruption?

options.label: A
options.text: It pre-scans a backup channel and moves there after radar
options.feedback: The backup has already completed CAC, reducing the interruption.

options.label: B
options.text: It disables radar detection on the active channel
options.feedback: Radar detection remains mandatory.

options.label: C
options.text: It sends every client to 2.4 GHz permanently
options.feedback: This is channel selection, not band disablement.

options.label: D
options.text: It stays on channel and lowers transmit power
options.feedback: Radar detection requires channel evacuation.

questions.question: A FortiGate WiFi event shows radar-detected. Which AP command best exposes Zero-Wait DFS state?

options.label: A
options.text: get system status
options.feedback: That reports platform details, not rCAC channel state.

options.label: B
options.text: diagnose sys sdwan health-check
options.feedback: That reports WAN probes, not DFS state.

options.label: C
options.text: execute sql-local rebuild-db
options.feedback: That is not an AP diagnostic.

options.label: D
options.text: cw_diag -c zwdfs
options.feedback: It reports radio mode and the pre-scanned frequency.

questions.question: An event shows the same channel before and after, but AP kernel logs show a move. Best interpretation?

options.label: A
options.text: The kernel log is always stale
options.feedback: AP diagnostics are direct evidence of radar processing.

options.label: B
options.text: The event field may have a known display issue
options.feedback: Correlate AP logs and release notes before concluding no move.

options.label: C
options.text: The AP ignored radar because channel IDs match
options.feedback: A repeated event value does not override radio evidence.

options.label: D
options.text: The client VLAN caused the channel display mismatch
options.feedback: VLAN assignment does not explain DFS event fields.

questions.question: FortiNAC shows an agent update pending, but no package reaches the endpoint. First communication test?

options.label: A
options.text: Reset every host's update counter immediately
options.feedback: Counters should be reset only after transport is corrected.

options.label: B
options.text: Verify host is online and Send Message works
options.feedback: Agent communication is a prerequisite for update.

options.label: C
options.text: Change endpoint DNS suffix to the NAC hostname
options.feedback: A suffix change does not prove agent communication.

options.label: D
options.text: Disable every compliance check before testing
options.feedback: That hides policy state without proving delivery.

questions.question: The agent remains on a loading screen while its icon is green. Which path is specifically required?

options.label: A
options.text: UDP 1812 from endpoint to RADIUS
options.feedback: RADIUS is not the package-delivery port.

options.label: B
options.text: TCP 22 from endpoint to FortiNAC
options.feedback: SSH is not the documented update transport.

options.label: C
options.text: TCP 80 from endpoint to FortiNAC
options.feedback: The guide requires HTTP port 80 for package delivery.

options.label: D
options.text: TCP 443 from FortiNAC to FortiAnalyzer
options.feedback: Log forwarding does not deliver the agent package.

questions.question: The global update target is lower than installed version. What does FortiNAC's comparison do?

options.label: A
options.text: It can install the different lower version when downgrade is allowed
options.feedback: The comparison is based on difference, not direction.

options.label: B
options.text: It always rejects any lower version number
options.feedback: The guide supports rollback to a previous version.

options.label: C
options.text: It waits until the host is reimaged
options.feedback: A normal agent connection can trigger comparison.

options.label: D
options.text: It updates only when target is newer semantically
options.feedback: That is not the documented comparison behavior.

questions.question: Many hosts exhausted attempts. After fixing TCP/80, what does Reset Counter do?

options.label: A
options.text: It deletes all Persistent Agent records
options.feedback: Reset Counter does not remove host inventory.

options.label: B
options.text: It installs packages on disconnected hosts
options.feedback: Hosts still must connect and communicate.

options.label: C
options.text: It clears attempts for failed hosts, not successful hosts
options.feedback: The guide says previously successful hosts are not re-updated.

options.label: D
options.text: It permanently disables the retry limit
options.feedback: It resets counts, not the retry control.

questions.question: A registered endpoint logs on and receives a tag, but a rogue device does not. Is that expected?

options.label: A
options.text: No, every IP in the subnet receives the same tag
options.feedback: Dynamic tags depend on registered host and policy state.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, rogue or offline hosts do not match the NAC policy
options.feedback: The policy path applies to registered, online devices.

options.label: C
options.text: No, tags are created only after firewall policy editing
options.feedback: The logon event triggers dynamic address synchronization.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only if FortiGate is DHCP server
options.feedback: The trigger is NAC identity, not DHCP server mode.

questions.question: FortiGate displays a FortiNAC dynamic address with a red exclamation mark. What does it indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: The endpoint certificate has expired
options.feedback: The marker reflects login mapping, not certificate validity.

options.label: B
options.text: The REST API is always disconnected
options.feedback: A red marker alone does not prove transport failure.

options.label: C
options.text: The group name contains unsupported spaces
options.feedback: The symbol is not a generic naming error.

options.label: D
options.text: No current logon is mapped to that dynamic address
options.feedback: The address has no matching current user/device login state.

questions.question: Two FSSO agents report the same endpoint IP. What risk is documented?

options.label: A
options.text: The later agent can overwrite the earlier login
options.feedback: FortiGate supports only one FSSO agent per endpoint IP.

options.label: B
options.text: FortiGate merges both identities into one tag
options.feedback: The documented behavior is overwrite, not union.

options.label: C
options.text: Both logins remain until firmware upgrade
options.feedback: The conflict is not deferred to firmware lifecycle.

options.label: D
options.text: The endpoint becomes a static address object
options.feedback: FSSO updates identity state, not static object type.

questions.question: FortiNAC-F loses contact with the Collector Agent. When are applicable SSO logins removed?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediately after the first delayed REST request
options.feedback: The documented timeout is five minutes.

options.label: B
options.text: After the endpoint renews its DHCP lease
options.feedback: DHCP lease renewal is not the disconnect timer.

options.label: C
options.text: After the fixed 300-second interval
options.feedback: FortiGate removes applicable SSO logins after five minutes.

options.label: D
options.text: Only after an administrator deletes the tag
options.feedback: The timeout provides automatic stale-login cleanup.

questions.question: An administrator revokes a certificate issued by the local CA. Where is revocation recorded?

options.label: A
options.text: In the FortiGate firewall policy log only
options.feedback: Policy logs do not maintain the issuer's CRL.

options.label: B
options.text: In the local CRL associated with the issuing CA
options.feedback: Revoking an end entity adds it to that CA's CRL.

options.label: C
options.text: In the OCSP responder DNS cache only
options.feedback: OCSP answers status; the CRL stores the revocation entry.

options.label: D
options.text: In the RADIUS accounting database
options.feedback: RADIUS accounting is unrelated to certificate revocation.

questions.question: FortiGate must query FortiAuthenticator's OCSP responder. Which detail is required?

options.label: A
options.text: A syslog destination on UDP 514
options.feedback: Syslog is not OCSP transport.

options.label: B
options.text: An LDAP bind with TCP 389
options.feedback: LDAP authentication does not query certificate status.

options.label: C
options.text: A CRL file path on the FortiGate interface
options.feedback: That is file-based checking, not OCSP.

options.label: D
options.text: The responder URL and certificate reference on TCP 2560
options.feedback: FortiAuthenticator documents OCSP on TCP port 2560.

questions.question: A certificate import event appears as log ID 10121. What does it establish?

options.label: A
options.text: A certificate-import operation occurred and may include an error
options.feedback: The event covers manual and CRL-related import activity.

options.label: B
options.text: Every TLS relying party accepted the certificate
options.feedback: Import success does not prove handshake acceptance.

options.label: C
options.text: The private key decrypted successfully
options.feedback: The event is not a key-decryption test.

options.label: D
options.text: The OCSP responder is reachable from every client
options.feedback: Import logs do not test all client paths.

questions.question: The certificate chain validates, but authentication fails during revocation checking. What should be isolated?

options.label: A
options.text: The FortiGate SD-WAN member priority
options.feedback: Routing preference does not establish certificate status.

options.label: B
options.text: The administrator GUI theme
options.feedback: Presentation settings do not affect revocation.

options.label: C
options.text: CRL/OCSP reachability, issuer match and freshness
options.feedback: Revocation is a separate check from chain trust.

options.label: D
options.text: The client's DHCPv6 IAID
options.feedback: Prefix delegation is unrelated to certificate revocation.

questions.question: A FortiPAM HA pair uses a custom private data encryption key. What key requirement applies?

options.label: A
options.text: Each node must use a unique key
options.feedback: The guide specifies the same key across HA members.

options.label: B
options.text: The same key must be present on all HA units
options.feedback: Key consistency is required for shared encrypted data.

options.label: C
options.text: The key can be omitted when restoring encrypted secrets
options.feedback: The target needs the key to decrypt secret material.

options.label: D
options.text: The key is only used for audit timestamps
options.feedback: The key protects passwords and private keys.

questions.question: A cross-platform FortiPAM migration is planned. Which source-side preparation is called out?

options.label: A
options.text: Convert the source to FortiSRA before exporting
options.feedback: Migration must remain between identical product types.

options.label: B
options.text: Upgrade source and target to different firmware builds
options.feedback: The procedure expects compatible firmware releases.

options.label: C
options.text: Disable Private Data Encryption before preparing the backup
options.feedback: The recent migration article lists source PDE disablement.

options.label: D
options.text: Delete all user accounts before creating the backup
options.feedback: Target seat capacity is checked; users are not simply deleted.

questions.question: A restore completes, but some users cannot be provisioned on target. Which preflight was missed?

options.label: A
options.text: The target user-seat capacity is insufficient
options.feedback: Migration guidance requires enough licensed seats for source users.

options.label: B
options.text: The source used a different dashboard layout
options.feedback: Dashboard layout does not determine licensing.

options.label: C
options.text: The backup was created during a weekday
options.feedback: The guide does not define weekday-only windows.

options.label: D
options.text: The target DNS server is not authoritative
options.feedback: DNS is not the stated seat-capacity prerequisite.

questions.question: The backup header identifies FortiPAM, but the target is FortiSRA. What should happen?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the product string and restore anyway
options.feedback: The migration guidance prohibits crossing product types.

options.label: B
options.text: Restore first and convert after reboot
options.feedback: Product identity is a pre-restore compatibility gate.

options.label: C
options.text: Import only launcher data and ignore product type
options.feedback: The backup must remain within the same product family.

options.label: D
options.text: Stop: FortiPAM and FortiSRA must not cross-migrate
options.feedback: The recent article explicitly requires identical product types.

questions.question: A Collector HA group is configured, but the VRRP VIP never appears on Leader. What should be checked?

options.label: A
options.text: The VIP is on a different subnet from Collectors
options.feedback: The documented VRRP design requires the same network.

options.label: B
options.text: The Supervisor owns the VIP instead of Collector
options.feedback: The Leader Collector owns the VIP.

options.label: C
options.text: The Collector uses a different Organization than its peer
options.feedback: HA members are selected from the same Organization.

options.label: D
options.text: The VIP and Collectors share the same network
options.feedback: The guide requires this for Collector HA.

questions.question: Two Collectors share an HA group. Which role assignment is valid?

options.label: A
options.text: One Leader has higher priority than each Follower
options.feedback: Only one Leader is allowed and it should outrank Followers.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Collectors are Leaders with equal priority
options.feedback: Only one Collector can be Leader.

options.label: C
options.text: Supervisor is Leader and both Collectors are Followers
options.feedback: Supervisor distributes jobs but does not own the VIP.

options.label: D
options.text: The VIP is assigned permanently to a Follower
options.feedback: The active Leader owns the VIP.

questions.question: The Leader process stops, but its OS remains up. Why might VRRP not fail over?

options.label: A
options.text: VRRP monitors application parsing latency
options.feedback: The documented caveat is node-level failure detection.

options.label: B
options.text: EPS decrease automatically disables the VIP
options.feedback: EPS does not itself trigger VRRP.

options.label: C
options.text: A process-only failure may not trigger node-level VRRP
options.feedback: Fortinet notes VRRP may not trigger when only a process stops.

options.label: D
options.text: Supervisor job placement prevents VIP movement
options.feedback: Job redistribution and VIP ownership are separate loops.

questions.question: Collector Health shows EPS=N/A, but tcpdump sees syslog packets. What conclusion is justified?

options.label: A
options.text: The Collector is definitely healthy because packets are visible
options.feedback: Packets may arrive while processing or forwarding fails.

options.label: B
options.text: Packets arrive; verify parsing and Analytics before declaring ingestion healthy
options.feedback: Packet arrival does not prove successful parsing or Analytics insertion.

options.label: C
options.text: The database must be corrupted and should be rebuilt
options.feedback: The Community article advises against backend changes based only on EPS=N/A.

options.label: D
options.text: The sender must change UDP port immediately
options.feedback: First correlate packet reception, processes and Analytics events.

questions.question: Internal DNS servers sit behind an SPA hub. Which FortiSASE access type should the DNS rule use?

options.label: A
options.text: Public, because all DNS queries originate from the PoP
options.feedback: Public uses WAN egress and misses the private SPA route.

options.label: B
options.text: Endpoint-local, so the resolver is bypassed
options.feedback: That would not send the query to internal DNS.

options.label: C
options.text: Private, so the query follows SPA/BGP path
options.feedback: Private is required when the resolver is reachable through SPA.

options.label: D
options.text: Proxy, because DNS redirection uses an explicit web proxy
options.feedback: Access Type is not an explicit web-proxy selection.

questions.question: Only internal suffixes should use corporate DNS; public names keep normal resolution. What feature fits?

options.label: A
options.text: Split DNS rules scoped to internal domains
options.feedback: Split DNS selectively sends specified suffixes to internal resolvers.

options.label: B
options.text: A global DNS override for every query
options.feedback: That sends public and internal queries to one resolver.

options.label: C
options.text: A full-tunnel steering rule for all endpoint traffic
options.feedback: Steering changes traffic path, not resolver selection by domain.

options.label: D
options.text: A static host entry pushed to every endpoint
options.feedback: Static hosts do not scale domain-based redirection.

questions.question: The DNS answer is correct, but the private service is unreachable behind SPA. What policy is easy to miss?

options.label: A
options.text: A FortiAnalyzer archive synchronization policy
options.feedback: Archive sync does not allow DNS traffic through SPA.

options.label: B
options.text: A FortiGate firmware template assigned to the resolver
options.feedback: Firmware management does not authorize DNS traffic.

options.label: C
options.text: A FortiNAC-F dynamic address tag for the resolver
options.feedback: Identity tags are not a substitute for DNS path permission.

options.label: D
options.text: A Private Access policy permitting DNS to that resolver
options.feedback: The server path must be allowed by Private Access policy.

questions.question: The deployment selects DNS over TCP/TLS, but the resolver is FortiGuard DNS. What limitation matters?

options.label: A
options.text: FortiGuard DNS requires all internal domains to use UDP 137
options.feedback: The documented limitation concerns TCP support.

options.label: B
options.text: FortiGuard DNS does not support DNS over TCP
options.feedback: Use a custom resolver that supports the selected transport.

options.label: C
options.text: FortiGuard DNS only resolves IPv6 PTR records
options.feedback: The resolver is general-purpose; the caveat concerns TCP.

options.label: D
options.text: FortiGuard DNS cannot serve remote endpoints
options.feedback: It is the default resolver for many SIA use cases.

questions.question: An SD-WAN health check needs TWAMP, but the GUI protocol list does not show it. Next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the protocol through the CLI health-check object
options.feedback: TWAMP is a CLI-selectable protocol in the Performance SLA guide.

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the health check with a firewall inspection profile
options.feedback: Policies do not select the SLA probe protocol.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable a FortiAnalyzer dataset for TWAMP metrics
options.feedback: Reports do not configure active probes.

options.label: D
options.text: Use DHCP option 82 to advertise the TWAMP server
options.feedback: Option 82 does not define SLA probes.

questions.question: FortiGate can ping the SLA target at 700 ms, but SLA reports dead. Which parameter likely explains it?

options.label: A
options.text: The link has no IPv4 default route
options.feedback: Successful ping suggests basic route reachability.

options.label: B
options.text: The SD-WAN zone name uses uppercase characters
options.feedback: Zone naming does not explain probe timeout.

options.label: C
options.text: The probe timeout is below measured round-trip time
options.feedback: A 500-ms default can mark a 700-ms response dead.

options.label: D
options.text: The FortiGate administrator profile lacks write permission
options.feedback: Admin permissions do not set SLA probe timing.

questions.question: A corporate-resource SLA should measure only IPsec overlays. Which participant design is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Include every WAN and LAN interface to increase samples
options.feedback: Unrelated interfaces can distort service-specific measurement.

options.label: B
options.text: Include only overlay members expected to carry the service
options.feedback: Participants should represent the actual service path.

options.label: C
options.text: Include the FortiAnalyzer management interface as control
options.feedback: Management reachability is not a data-plane participant.

options.label: D
options.text: Include only the preferred member and remove all others
options.feedback: That prevents comparison among eligible paths.

questions.question: A member has two health checks. One fails while one remains alive. What happens to its routes?

options.label: A
options.text: Routes are removed as soon as either check fails
options.feedback: All configured checks must fail before route removal.

options.label: B
options.text: The member stays removed until an administrator re-enables it
options.feedback: Eligibility follows health-check recovery.

options.label: C
options.text: The member moves to another zone automatically
options.feedback: Health checks do not rewrite zone membership.

options.label: D
options.text: It remains eligible because not all checks failed
options.feedback: All configured checks must fail before removal from the group.

questions.question: A NAT64 policy matches, but the server reply never returns. Which path should be verified after translation?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the DNS64 cache TTL on the client
options.feedback: TTL does not prove translated IPv4 return routing.

options.label: B
options.text: IPv4 route and server return path for the pool source
options.feedback: The server must route replies to the translated source through the stateful path.

options.label: C
options.text: The AP's DFS NOL list and radio channel
options.feedback: Wireless channel state is unrelated to the IPv4 return path.

options.label: D
options.text: The FortiManager template schedule
options.feedback: Firmware scheduling does not affect the NAT64 session.

questions.question: A remote SASE user resolves a private FQDN, but security inspection blocks it as Newly Observed Domain. What should be investigated?

options.label: A
options.text: The DNS rule spelling only
options.feedback: Resolution already succeeded; the remaining block may be filtering.

options.label: B
options.text: The FortiSIEM Collector VIP priority
options.feedback: Collector HA does not govern SASE web filtering.

options.label: C
options.text: A narrow Web Filter or DNS Filter exception
options.feedback: A correct DNS answer can still be blocked by security inspection.

options.label: D
options.text: The FortiSwitch BPDU guard timeout
options.feedback: Spanning-tree protection does not affect SASE categorization.
